With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal by the appellants under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 22.12.2021 passed by Member IInd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Betul in MCC No.127/2016 seeking reduction of compensation amount as well as exoneration from liability to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellants submit that Manoj was not owner of offending vehicle on the date of accident.
He had sold offending vehicle prior to accident i.e. approximately 10 years before accident occurred.

With the permission of this Court, learned counsel for the appellants submits that in view of injuries sustained by respondent/claimant in the accident as well as nature of permanent disability, it cannot be said that claimant suffered any loss of future earning capacity.
Therefore, Tribunal wrongly granted Rs.2,37,600/- for loss of future earning capacity.
On above grounds, appeal filed by the appellants be allowed.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent/claimant after referring impugned award as well as disability certificate Ex.P/258 and deposition of Dr.Ramesh Badwe submits that on account of injuries claimant has suffered permanent disabilities and it has adversely effected memory.

Therefore,
Tribunal has rightly granted compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
5. I have learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

6. So far as,liability to pay compensation/ownership of offending vehicle on the date of accident is concerned, admittedly, on the date of accident, appellant Manoj was a registered owner of offending vehicle.
It is well settled that claimant can claim compensation from registered owner as well as actual owner of vehicle.
In this connection, tribunal has also referred relevant pronouncement in para 30 of impugned award.

7. Therefore, in this Court's considered opinion, tribunal has not committed any illegality and has rightly fastened liability on appellant Manoj to pay the compensation as he was registered owner of offending vehicle on the date of accident.
8. So far as amount of compensation is concerned, claimant has filed permanent disability certificate Ex.P/258 and has examined Dr.Ramesh to prove the same.
As per Dr.Ramesh Badwe, he is not a neuro expert and instead he is a surgical specialist.
This Court has gone through the Ex.P/258 and deposition of Dr.Ramesh Badwe and has examined the same.

Claimant has not examined any neuro expert to prove that on account of injuries sustained in the accident that claimant has lost/adversely effected memory etc. or has suffered any kind of mental disorder .
Dr.Ramesh has not deposed that claimant has suffered any other kind of permanent disability on account of injury sustained in the accident.
9. As per medical evidence available on record, claimant suffered injuries on face/jaw etc and on date of accident claimant was aged 21 years.

10. In view of overall evidence on record, in this Court's considered opinion, tribunal has wrongly held that there is loss of future earning capacity and has wrongly awarded amount under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
But in view of injuries sustained by the claimant on her face etc., it would be just and proper to award an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- for the same.
11. In view of above, appeal filed by the appellants is partly allowed and compensation awarded by Tribunal is reduced by Rs.87,600/-.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
